references.text: Describes the priestly garments to be made for Aaron and his sons, including the sash and turbans mentioned in the consecration ceremony.
Instructions on making tunics, sashes, and turbans for Aaron's sons, and consecrating them for priestly service.
Moses performs the consecration of Aaron and his sons by clothing them in priestly garments, establishing a perpetual priesthood.
The execution of the consecration where Moses ties sashes around Aaron's sons and places turbans on their heads.
Priestly service is given as a gift and a permanent arrangement to Aaron and his sons.
The expression 'to fill the hand' (מִלֵּא יָד) is used regarding consecration for service to the Lord.
Describes the seven-day consecration period during which the hands of Aaron and his sons were filled for priestly service.
Contrasts the temporary Levitical priesthood with Christ's eternal priesthood.
Both verses describe the installation ritual where clothing and anointing lead to a perpetual priesthood.
The verse summarizes and confirms the timeframe of the installation process, of which the clothing in v. 9 is a part.
The source describes the use of the garment, while this verse describes the purpose of making it (glory and beauty).
Complementary verses that together show that both clothing and anointing are necessary to establish priestly service.
Both verses define the boundaries of the priesthood: 29:9 through installation, and 3:10 through exclusivity and the death penalty for intruders.
28:43 explains the life-or-death consequence of the garment mandated in 29:9.
Confirms that clothing and anointing are inseparable parts of the sanctification that enables priestly service.
